title: Review of Enforcement Measures Against Pet Groomers and Proposal for Mandatory CCTV Recordings in Pet Grooming Facilities
what_it_is: Review of Enforcement Measures Against Pet Groomers and Proposal for Mandatory CCTV Recordings in Pet Grooming Facilities

sections.label: Pet business enforcement and penalties
sections.summary: Measures against non-compliant pet businesses are being reviewed, including penalties, licence suspensions and possible CCTV requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what measures are being taken to strengthen enforcement against pet businesses, including pet grooming facilities, that fail to comply with the Animals and Birds Act (ABA) and Code of Animal Welfare; and (b) whether under the review of the ABA, serious negligence by pet businesses causing animal harm or death may result in enhanced penalties or longer licence suspensions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Hence, these individuals face higher maximum penalties under the Animals and Birds Act (ABA) for animal cruelty and welfare offences compared to other members of the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Upon conviction for an animal welfare offence, the Court may also issue a disqualification order to an individual to disqualify them from owning an animal or running an animal-related business for up to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The National Parks Board (NParks) has investigated 54 cases of feedback alleging harm to pets caused by groomers over the past three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We are reviewing the regulatory regime for pet sector activities, including pet grooming businesses, under the ongoing review of the ABA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We will consider whether to include requirements for closed circuit television (CCTV) recordings when we amend the legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We are also reviewing the appropriate penalties for animal welfare and cruelty offences, including those that apply to animal-related businesses.

sections.label: Code of Animal Welfare breaches
sections.summary: The Code sets minimum standards for pet businesses and groomers, and breaches can support prosecution under the ABA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: With regard to the Code for Animal Welfare, which I mentioned earlier on, this is for specific to the pet industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: This Code of Animal Welfare specifies minimum standards and best practices for pet businesses and pet groomers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: All pet groomers are encouraged to comply with these sets of standards and best practices, and that includes not leaving animals unattended in rooms, unsupervised, as the Member had mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But where there are breaches to this code, they can be used to support prosecution under the ABA and where unnecessary pain or suffering has been found to be inflicted on the animal, that is section 42 of the ABA, or failure of duty of care is found, section 41 of the ABA, NParks then can take an appropriate enforcement action under ABA.
